text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
SABAH
- Independent deputy Yalim Erez, has been asked to become leader of the conservative Democrat Turkey Party.
- Kurdish rebel leader Abdullah Ocalan and his brother are wanted by the state to enroll for military service.
MILLIYET
- Former Islamist minister Abdullah Gul accuses the military of mounting a coup.
- People from the poverty-stricken southeast go to northern Black Sea region, for the hazelnut harvest, hoping to find work.
HURRIYET
- Parliament is to vote on a critical secularist eight-year education bill on Thursday.
- Istanbul Chamber of Commerce will set up a holding company to sponsor the new education plan by around $6 billion.
YENI YUZYIL
- Fugutive businessman Asil Nadir secretly flew to Turkish Cyprus on Wednesday night, despite a ban on his leaving Turkey for tax debts.
- The Turkish casino sector is considering transfering its bases to the Central Asian Turkic republics and Russia as casinos are to be shut down in Turkey.
CUMHURIYET
- Parliament passes bill for partial amnesty on newspaper editors imprisoned for political crimes.
- Security measures are tightened in southeast on the 13th anniversary of separatist Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) beginning its campaign against the state.
RADIKAL
- Two military pilots died when an F4 warplane crashed in central Turkey.
ZAMAN
- Turkey is planning to produce its own strike helicopter prototype before the year 2,000.
